message.text:
**Evaluating function calls**

I need to determine the fan-in for internal functions, which is pretty tricky since scanning the call graph manually feels impossible. I’m thinking it’s likely related to some internal utility functions that are frequently called. I should compute a static approximation using scripts, searching for declarations under internal and counting the identifiers. It might help to inspect `util.GetEnv`. I could write a Perl script to extract and count function declarations without writing to files, also keeping method collisions in mind.

args.command: perl -e 'sub walk{my($d)=@_;opendir(my $h,$d)||return;for my $f(readdir $h){next if $f eq "."||$f eq "..";my$p="$d/$f";if(-d$p){walk($p)}elsif($p=~/\.go$/){open my$x,"<",$p||next;my$n=0;while(<$x>){$n++;print "$p:$n:$_" if /^func\s+(?:\([^)]*\)\s*)?(\w+)\s*\(/}}}closedir$h}walk("internal")'

perl -e 'sub files{my($d)=@_;my@o;opendir(my$h,$d)||return@o;for my$f(readdir$h){next if$f eq"."||$f eq"..";my$p="$d/$f";if(-d$p){push@o,files($p)}elsif($p=~/\.go$/&&!$p=~/_test\.go$/){push@o,$p}}closedir$h;@o}my@all=files(".");my%decl;for my$p(files("internal")){open my$f,"<",$p;my$n=0;while(<$f>){$n++;if(/^func\s+(?:\([^)]*\)\s*)?(\p{Alpha}\w*)\s*\(/){$decl{$1}="$p:$n"}}}my%txt;for my$p(@all){open my$f,"<",$p;while(<$f>){for my$name(keys%decl){$txt{$name}+=()=/\b\Q$name\E\b/g}}}for my$name(sort{$txt{$b}<=>$txt{$a}}keys%decl){printf "%4d %-28s %s\n",$txt{$name}-1,$name,$decl{$name} if $txt{$name}>2}'

message.text:
**Troubleshooting code issues**

I’m thinking about bug precedence and it seems like there might be a glob issue with internal functions. I'm reflecting on the use of Perl's `\p`, which appears to be fine. However, I need a simpler solution in Python but it's not available right now. Should I consider using awk instead? I need to make sure I fix that Perl line `($p ! /_test/)` properly to resolve the issue.
